authorization: Owner request of 2026-10-14 16:23Z (project thread «Noche abierta: nivel A0 y voces», from the «Clase inicial A0» thread): add an A0 level to Noche abierta that is literally A0 and fully bilingual, with bilingual new words at A0–A2. This manifest approves only the exact English support literals of that A0 level listed below (the English half of each { es, en } pair in the A0 content files); existing English copy stays protected. Owner approval line («apruebo») recorded in the same thread.

additions.text: It is Saturday. It is night. Today is Vale’s birthday. There is a party. Walk and go in wherever you want.
Do you like parties? Yes or no?
It is raining. The square and the rooftop are empty. There are no taxis.
Which place is good in the rain: the café, the bar or the square?
Where are you going now? Say one place.
Do you have an umbrella? Yes or no?
There is no metro. There is no bus. Lu wants to go home.
Does Lu go by taxi or on foot?
Are you going home now? Yes or no?
Nico doesn’t have his phone. Where is it?
Where are you tonight? Say one place.
Is the phone at the bar, in the taxi or in the square?
Do you look for the phone? Yes or no?
Where did you go? Say one place.
What is there in that place?
Who is a person from tonight? Say their name.
Do you like the night? Yes or no?
You are at the café. The waitress asks: “Here or to go?”
You want the coffee to go. What do you say?
What do you drink: coffee, tea or water?
You order a tea. The waitress brings a coffee.
Tea or coffee? With milk or without milk?
You walk into the café with two friends. You are three people.
Who do you have coffee with?
You are at Vale’s home. You are thirsty.
Are you coming to my house?
What is your home like: big or small?
You are at Vale’s door. You ring the bell. Vale asks: “Who is it?”
Hi, I’m Alex. I’m at the door.
You eat with friends. The bill comes. You want to pay only for your food.
What do you eat at a restaurant?
You want a soup without meat.
Do you eat meat? Yes or no?
It is very noisy. You want another table.
Do you like noise? Yes or no?
My name is Alex. And you?
What is your name? Where are you from?
Inés says: “I’m new in the neighbourhood.”
Where do you live? Is it nice?
Ana and Diego say: “Let’s go dancing!” You are hungry.
Do you like dancing? Yes or no?
Ramiro asks: “Where is the station?” The station is on the right.
How do you go to work: by bus, by car or on foot?
Kenji says: “I don’t understand. Can you repeat?”
Which Spanish word do you like?
Sofía says: “Shall we go listen to music?” You want to go.
The music is very loud. You can’t hear your friend.
Shall we go to a quiet table?
Shall we sit next to the speaker?
You are at the bar. You are sleepy.
What time do you go to sleep?
You have no cash. You have a card.
Do you pay by card or with cash?
You wait at the bar. Someone asks: “Are you in the line?”
No, I’m looking for the exit.
Do you wait a lot in your city? Where?
Your friends want to go to another bar. It is very expensive.
Shall we order the most expensive thing?
Expensive or cheap? Which do you prefer?
Nico writes: “I can’t today.” You want to see him tomorrow.
I’ll wait for you here today.
Sergio arrives at the bar. There is a free chair next to you.
What do you say when a friend arrives?
The car won’t start. You need to go to the airport.
Do you travel by plane? Where to?
The car needs petrol. A neighbour walks by.
Where is there a petrol station?
Do you have a car? What colour?
You look at an old photo. You want to know the year.
Do you take photos? Of what?
You see an old telephone. How does it work?
Who do you talk to on the phone?
You see an old train ticket.
Where do you want to travel?
You see an old letter. The writing is very small.
Can I write on the letter?
Do you write letters or messages?
You see an old suitcase. What is it made of?
What do you carry in your suitcase? Say three things.
You see an old TV. Does it work?
Do you watch TV? What do you watch?
You see a postman’s bicycle. You don’t know the word “cartero”.
Where do I buy a stamp?
Do you have a bicycle? Yes or no?
You see an old room. There is a strange object.
What time does the tour start?
You see a music box. It is closed.
Can we listen to the music?
Can we turn off the light?
You are in a taxi. The street is closed.
I go by taxi to the rooftop.
Do you take taxis? Yes or no?
The taxi is going to the square. The driver asks: “Do I keep going?”
Let’s go back to the taxi stand.
You are at the shop. Your charger doesn’t fit the socket.
What do you use your phone for?
You buy ice. You want to take it home cold.
What do you buy at the shop?
You are looking for a gift for a friend. She likes tea.
You are on the rooftop with friends. You want to stay here.
Shall we stay a bit longer?
What do you do at night?
You want a photo with your friends.
Shall we go down the stairs?
Who do you take photos with?
Pencil. Write, draw, leave a note.
Book. Look things up, show, give.
Pepper spray. In case you feel in danger.
Grenade. Nobody knows if it is real. Nobody wants to find out.
Gun. Everyone sees it before they see you.
Knife. Cut, open… or someone pulls out theirs.
Heart. A power: it changes the mood of whoever receives it.
You come back with the pharmacist. Don Teodoro is awake. Ofelia hugs you.
The ambulance arrives. Don Teodoro gets in. Ofelia waves goodbye.
Don Teodoro is sitting up and drinks water. Ofelia hugs him.
Do you call an ambulance in your country? What number is it?
An old man is on the ground. His daughter shouts: “Help! My dad!”
Ofelia says: “Yes! It’s there, on the corner.”
The man opens his eyes. “What… what’s happening?”
You have a newspaper. Don Amadeo smiles.
You close the newsstand together. “See you tomorrow.”
Do you read the news? Where?
A man is closing his newsstand. “Good evening! Do you want a newspaper?”
Don Amadeo gives you a newspaper. “It’s free. It’s the last one.”
Don Amadeo smiles. “Yes! This box, please.”
You have a ticket for Saturday. Abril is happy.
Abril writes down your idea and leaves happy.
A girl looks at a film poster. There is an octopus on a bus. “Hi. Do you like it?”
“On Saturday there is a screening. Are you coming?”
I can’t. But the octopus is the driver.
Abril writes in her notebook. “Good idea!”
The ambulance arrives. Rolo leaves. Vanesa stays with her car.
The police arrive. Vanesa cries. Rolo explains everything.
Rolo has the paper with the details. Vanesa drives away slowly.
Vanesa pushes you again. A neighbour stops her. It’s chaos.
Do you ride a bicycle? Yes or no?
A car and a bicycle. The boy has blood on his head. The woman shouts: “It’s not my fault!”
Vanesa shouts: “No! It’s not my fault!”
Rolo says: “I need her name and her phone number.”
Madam, your name and phone number, please.
Vanesa writes on a piece of paper. “Here.”
Kevin dances. He watches the video many times.
Kevin is on the ground, but he laughs. “Tomorrow!”
Do you do sports? Which one?
A boy with a skateboard says: “Hi! Can you film me with my phone?”
Kevin gives you the phone. “Thanks! Watch.”
No, sorry. I’m in a hurry.
Kevin jumps with the skateboard. Oops!
Ulises closes the door. He is a bit angry.
Ulises turns on a light. The yellow dot shines.
A black painting with a yellow dot. A man asks: “What do you see?”
You leave. The music goes on. Elena is angry.
The music goes down. Elena goes back home.
Elena joins the party and dances. Everyone sings “Happy birthday”.
The police arrive. The party ends. Gonzalo is sad.
Do you listen to loud music at home?
There is very loud music. A neighbour in pyjamas shouts: “It’s very late! I want to sleep!”
Elena says: “It’s not normal!” and leaves.
A guy opens the door. “Hi! It’s my birthday! Is there a problem?”
Happy birthday! Shall we come in?
Gonzalo laughs. “Come in!” Elena comes in too.
You see a huge lamp and red carpets.
Sebastián winks at you and opens the door for a guest.
Sebastián looks at the street. Serious again.
What clothes are you wearing today?
A doorman in a red uniform. “Good evening. Are you a hotel guest?”
No. Can I see the hotel?
Sebastián opens the door. “One moment. Just a look.”
No. Your uniform is very elegant.
Sebastián smiles. “Thanks. There are famous people inside…”
Don Emilio calls his grandson. You wait with him.
You leave. Don Emilio keeps searching.
Don Emilio opens his car and drives away slowly.
Don Emilio gets into the taxi. “Bye!”
What colour is your car or your family’s car?
An old man searches among the cars. “Sorry… I can’t find my car.”
There is a small red car over there. “Is it that one?”
Don Emilio opens the car. “Thanks!” He gives you a sweet.
A taxi arrives. Don Emilio says goodbye.
You drink the grape juice. It’s very tasty.
You have a card with the name of a wine.
Renata goes back into the wine shop. You keep walking.
What do you drink at dinner?
A woman at the door of a wine shop. “Hi! Do you want to try? There is wine and there is grape juice, alcohol-free.”
Renata gives you a glass. “It’s tasty!”
Renata writes a name on a card. “This one.”
The police arrive. Carolina talks to them. Mateo sits down.
The ambulance takes Mateo away. Carolina goes with him.
Nobody shouts. That’s enough for today.
Do you shout when you are angry?
A woman shouts: “My phone!” A man has blood on his arm. She says to you: “You! Help!”
Mateo says: “My arm hurts. A lot.”
Mateo says: “Thanks.” Carolina goes with him.
Carolina sits down. Mateo looks at the ground. Silence.
The keys are in the mailbox. Don Manolo closes the balcony door.
Don Manolo has his keys. He turns on the light and waves.
The basket goes up with the keys. Don Manolo laughs and claps.
Where do you put your keys at home?
A man on a balcony. “Sorry! My keys are there, on the ground.”
Here they are! Shall I throw them?
I’ll leave them in the mailbox.
Don Manolo says: “Okay…” and closes the balcony door.
You throw the keys. Up! Don Manolo catches them.
Don Manolo says: “Thanks!” and turns on the light.
Don Manolo laughs. “Yes! A basket. What an idea!”
Nilda leaves with her cart. The inspector writes down your description.
Nilda sells tonight. Tomorrow, the permit. You have two tamales.
Nilda puts away the fine. She leaves slowly with her cart.
What street food is there in your city?
A woman runs with a tamale cart. An inspector shouts: “Stop! You have no permit!”
The inspector says: “No permit, a fine.”
Nilda says: “It’s my job. Tomorrow I’ll ask for the permit.”
No fine today. Tomorrow, permit. Yes?
The inspector says: “…All right. Tomorrow at eight.” Nilda gives you two tamales.
I’m sorry. It’s not my problem.
The inspector writes the fine. Nilda walks away slowly.
You have dinner with Nieves’s family. They talk a lot and laugh.
Nieves says goodbye. The window is still lit.
Who do you have dinner with?
A lit window. A family is having dinner. A grandmother says: “Hi! Are you hungry? Come in!”
Yes, thank you. Just a moment.
You have dinner with the family. Everyone talks and laughs.
No, thank you. Enjoy your meal!
Henrik goes to the station. He is happy.
You go with Henrik to the market. He talks about his grandmother.
Henrik goes to the market. He is very hungry.
A guy with a map. “Sorry… Where is the station?”
Straight ahead and to the left.
Henrik shows you the map. “Here. And the market?”
Yes. It’s there, on the right.
You go with Leire, Óscar and Mavi to La Fábrica. Everyone laughs.
The three leave singing. Leire waves goodbye with the flowers.
Óscar dances in the square. Leire and Mavi dance. And you!
Do you like dancing? What music?
Three friends leave a hotel. A girl with flowers says: “Hi! Are you coming to a party?”
Leire says: “At La Fábrica. Let’s go!”
Leire says: “Bye!” The three of them sing.
Óscar says: “Yes! And now, let’s dance!” And he dances in the square.
You have a very pretty bouquet. “Good luck,” says Doña Mirta.
You have a flower. You are happy.
A woman with flowers. “Good evening. Flowers? For whom?”
Doña Mirta makes a bouquet. “Here. Good luck!”
Doña Mirta gives you a flower. “This one is free.”
You have a paper with numbers. It is your future.
Madame Zulema tells you about her life. You laugh a lot.
What do you want to do next year?
A woman with cards at a table. “Come. Do you want to know your future?”
Madame Zulema looks at the cards. “A trip. And a number: seven.”
Madame Zulema laughs. “Me neither. I’m a maths teacher.”
Iker and Canelo say goodbye. Canelo doesn’t bark anymore.
Canelo sleeps. Iker turns off the light.
Do you have a pet? Which one?
A dog barks on a balcony. A man says: “Sorry! Canelo, quiet!”
Iker smiles. Canelo wags his tail.
He barks a lot. The neighbours are sleeping.
Iker says: “Yes, sorry.” Canelo falls asleep.
You leave. Joaquín tells the news to someone else.
Joaquín records a message for his family. He talks and laughs.
Joaquín opens his arms. Very happy. You too.
Which country do you want to visit?
A guy jumps and shouts: “I got a scholarship! I’m going to study in Japan!”
“But… Japan is far away. I’m scared.”
That’s normal. You can do it!
Joaquín opens his arms. Very happy.
